Orrin.narrative: I keep the watch because someone must make the rules mean something when tempers rise. Brandholm owes Saltreach, and I will not call it fair trade while their debts sit unpaid and our stores come up short. I know Maelis has the Tally, not the command; still, I will argue with her until the council acts.
goals: Find whoever is taking smoked fish from the Storehouse.
Get Brandholm's debts paid, even if trade must stop until they are.
Keep the watch respected and Saltreach safe.
Orrin.mood: Irritable, watchful, and impatient with delay.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She works harder than anyone, though I wish she would stand with me more plainly.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants to fish with the men; I want him to learn patience first.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows Posy everywhere and thinks the whole world is a game.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He speaks for the hired hands as if the council can be pulled apart without cost.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She worries when Cade and I quarrel, though she knows I have duties.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: rival
relations.note: Her writing can stall a decision that ought to be made aloud and acted on.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She knows what Brandholm took from her, and she does not soften it.

relations.name: Tobin
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: He is grim, but I trust him to keep at a hard task.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: watchman
relations.note: Fast on his feet and cheerful; I need him to take the work seriously.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes more than anyone and acts as if the Tally is a personal insult.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: wife's hand
relations.note: She works hard at Bea's racks, but I don't like how quickly she and Lark turn every grievance into a cause.

memories.gist: I was a boy when the Hunger Winter took two of my mother's children. I remember the cold and how little a promise mattered beside an empty pot.
When the Net-Council named me Captain of the Watch, I took the charge as a duty, not an honour to show off.
The council told me to find the hand taking smoked fish. I left that meeting angry that the stores could be short and no one could say why.
I argued with Maelis over Brandholm's debts and left the Storehouse no closer to a decision than when I entered.

stances.why: A debt left unpaid teaches every household that the Tally can be ignored.
A warning that nobody respects is just noise.
The Storehouse belongs to the whole town, and theft makes every share less certain.
Waiting for perfect agreement lets harm become ordinary.

Bea.narrative: I run the Smokehouse by heat, timing, and the hands that show up when they are paid. Oriel and Lark do good work, and I give them the marks and fish we agreed on each market morning. I have noticed smoked fish missing after dark; Orrin wants an answer, but shouting does not make one appear.
goals: Keep the Smokehouse working well and its workers paid as agreed.
Find out why fish goes missing without putting blame on the wrong person.
Keep Orrin's anger from making every disagreement worse.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He cares about Saltreach, but his shouting wears the whole house thin.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is eager to be grown; I want him to learn the work before he takes risks.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has found a way to follow Posy into every corner.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: hand
relations.note: She works steadily beside me, and I mean to pay her what we agreed.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: hand
relations.note: Quick with a joke and quick with the racks; she should not have to beg for a voice.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: She keeps the shares straight, even when Orrin and I wish the answers were simpler.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He is calmer than Orrin and speaks for people who do hard work without a council seat.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: ally
relations.note: She has reason to be angry with the north, though anger can spread too far.

relations.name: Mara
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She worries over both her sons, and I wish she could get Orrin to hear himself when he shouts.

memories.gist: I learned to judge the smoke by smell and color; one careless turn of the racks can spoil a day's work.
After dark I noticed the smoked fish was short again. I checked the racks and the count, then had to admit I still did not know where it went.
On a market morning I counted out the agreed marks and fish for Oriel and Lark. I want our bargains to stay clear, even when the stores are strained.
Orrin came home angry about Brandholm's debts. I agreed they were taking advantage, but I could not make myself believe that anger alone would settle it.

stances.why: A spoken bargain is worth keeping even when the work is hard.
A guess can ruin an innocent person's name and still leave the stores short.
Their debts linger while Saltreach has to keep counting what it can spare.
People hear the anger and stop hearing the useful part.

Dag.narrative: I want to fish with the men and bring back something worth counting. Father says there is more to it than wanting, and Mother says I should learn the work before I boast. I like being with Ness, but I do not want to be treated like a little child.
goals: Learn enough fishing to go out with the men.
Show Father I can be trusted with real work.
Spend time with Ness without everyone making a fuss.
Dag.mood: Restless and eager to prove myself.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is always watching the watch, and I want him to watch me do something well.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows when I'm hungry before I say it.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is little, but she follows me around when she is not following Posy.

relations.name: Ness
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She talks to me like I'm nearly grown, which is how it should be.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She and Lotte make games out of everything, even when I have better things to do.

memories.gist: I watched the fishers ready their gear and asked when I could come. Father told me wanting to go was not the same as being ready.
Ness and I talked while the adults were busy. She did not tell me to go play, and I liked that.
Mother showed me how to mind the fire around the fish. I tried not to look pleased when she said I had done it properly.

stances.why: You cannot become useful if nobody lets you try.
Father says the sea does not care how eager you are.
It is tiresome when people decide what you can do without asking.

Lotte.narrative: Mother's smoke smells warm, and Father has a loud voice. Dag is big and knows things, but he does not always play. Posy is fun to follow.
goals: Stay close to Mother when the Smokehouse is busy.
Get Dag to play with me.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: father
relations.note: His voice is big, but he is my father.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells like smoke and fish, and I like being where she is.

relations.name: Dag
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is big enough to reach things for me, if he remembers.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: friend
relations.note: I follow her because she always finds a game.

memories.gist: I followed Posy across the market square and Mother called us back before we got too far.
